## Setting and conventions

- [P] Introduction (p. 189): `X` is an `n x n` alternating matrix (`x_ii = 0` and `x_ij = -x_ji`) with entries in a commutative ring `R` with identity; its Pfaffian `Pf(X)` is `0` for odd `n`, and for even `n` `Pf(X)^2 = det X`. Deleting the rows and columns with indices
  `i_1, ..., i_k` leaves an alternating matrix whose Pfaffian is written `Pf^(i_1 ... i_k)(X)`, of order `n - k`; `Pf_(2p)(X)` is the ideal generated by the Pfaffians of order `2p`. The paper bounds the height and the depth of `Pf_(2p)(X)` by
  `mu(p, n) = (n - 2p + 1)(n - 2p + 2)/2` and shows the bound attained for algebraically independent entries under a flatness hypothesis; Section 3 gives a free resolution of `Pf_(n-2)(X)` of length 6.

## Reduction lemmas (Section 1, pp. 190-191)

- [P] Lemma 1.1 (p. 190): the Laplace expansion of `Pf(X)` along a fixed index `j` is the signed sum of the entries `x_ij` times the Pfaffians `Pf^(ij)(X)` of the matrix with rows and columns `i` and `j` removed.
  Lemma 1.2 (p. 190): if `x_12` is invertible in `R` there is an invertible matrix `C` with `C^t X C` equal to the block matrix of the standard `2 x 2` alternating block and an `(n-2) x (n-2)` alternating matrix `X'` whose entries are
  `x_ij` plus a correction quotient by `x_12` built from `x_1i`, `x_2i`, `x_1j`, `x_2j`, and `Pf_(2p)(X) = Pf_(2(p-1))(X')` for `p >= 1`.
- [P] Corollary 1.3 (p. 191): over a local ring, if `Pf_(n-2)(X) = R` then an invertible matrix `C` brings `X` to a block matrix of `2 x 2` standard blocks followed by one block `a` times the standard block, for some `a` in `R`.

## Height and depth (Section 2, pp. 191-193)

- [P] Theorem 2.1 (p. 191): for a commutative Noetherian ring `R` with identity and an `n x n` alternating matrix `X` over `R`, every minimal prime ideal of `Pf_(2p)(X)` has height at most `mu(p, n)`. The proof is sketched by induction on `n`, with Krull's generalized principal ideal theorem for `n <= 2` or `p = 1`,
  the reduction of Lemma 1.2 when some entry is invertible, and the argument of Eagon and Northcott (reference [5], pp. 202-203) after adjoining a polynomial variable `t` otherwise.
- [P] Corollary 2.2 (p. 192): under the hypotheses of Theorem 2.1, `depth Pf_(2p)(X) <= mu(p, n)`. Theorem 2.3 (p. 192): for a Noetherian ring `S` and a Noetherian subring `R` with the same identity, a family `{x_ij}`, `1 <= i < j <= n`, of elements of `S` algebraically independent over `R` with `S` flat over `R[{x_ij}]`, and `X` the alternating matrix
  with these entries, `depth Pf_(2p)(X) = mu(p, n)`. The proof (pp. 192-193) is an induction on `n` and `p` that inverts an entry outside a prime `P` associated to a maximal regular sequence in `Pf_(2p)(X)` and applies Lemma 1.2 and a lemma on algebraic independence after localization (Lemma 2.4).
- [P] Corollary 2.5 (p. 193): for a commutative Noetherian ring `R` and the polynomial ring `S = R[{x_ij}]` in `(n^2 - n)/2` indeterminates, `depth Pf_(2p)(X) = mu(p, n)` for the generic alternating matrix `X`; Remark 2.6: Kleppe proved this independently when `R` is a field. Corollary 2.7: for a local algebra `S` over a field `K` in which the `x_ij` form a regular sequence, `depth Pf_(2p)(X) = mu(p, n)`.

## A free resolution of the ideal of Pfaffians of order n - 2 (Section 3, pp. 193-197)

- [P] Pages 193-194: for even `n`, with `Y` the adjugate-type alternating matrix of the `(n-2)`-Pfaffians (`XY = YX = Pf(X) E` by Lemma 1.1), `L(X)` is a self-dual complex of free `R`-modules of length 6, built from the matrices `M_n(R)` modulo the symmetric and the alternating matrices, the trace map and the identity, with
  `H_0(L(X)) = R/Pf_(n-2)(X)`. Theorem 3.2 (p. 194): for a commutative Noetherian ring `R` in which 2 is invertible and an `n x n` alternating `X` with `n` even, if `depth Pf_(n-2)(X) = 6` (the largest possible) then `L(X)` is acyclic and is a free resolution of `R/Pf_(n-2)(X)`. The proof (pp. 196-197, after Lemmas 3.3 and 3.4 on pp. 194-196) reduces by localization, Lemma 3.3, Corollary 1.3 and Lemma 3.4 to a normal form
  and verifies exactness by hand; the page notes that the complex is not exact when `R` has characteristic 2, since the proof uses the invertibility of 2.
- [P] Corollary 3.6 (p. 197): over a local ring in which 2 is invertible, `Pf_(n-2)(X)` is a Gorenstein ideal for every alternating `X` with `depth Pf_(n-2)(X) = 6`. Remark 3.7 (p. 197): that all Pfaffians are Gorenstein under generic hypotheses in characteristic 0 was proved in a note of the same authors (reference [7]), and
  the characteristic 0 assumption can be dropped (information attributed to D. Laksov).
- [P] Corollary 3.8 (p. 197): for a field `K` with `char K != 2`, the complex `L(T)` is a free `R`-resolution of `R/I`, where `T` is the generic `6 x 6` alternating matrix over `R = K[{t_ij}]` and `I = Pf_4(T)` is the ideal defining the Grassmannian `G(2, 6)` of 2-dimensional subspaces of `K^6` (introduction, p. 190: the resolution of the ideal of this Grassmannian is an application).

## Mapping to this repository

- [I] The A_5 fiber-cone program ([run rulebook](../../runbooks/run-rulebook.md), ledger rows A5-416, A5-418 and A5-421 in `docs/evidence/a5-exceptional-fibers/ledger.tsv`) works with ideals generated by 4-Pfaffians of an alternating matrix whose entries are specialized
  (the rows state 126 principal four-Pfaffians of a Schur-form matrix). Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 hold over an arbitrary commutative Noetherian ring, so they apply to every specialization and to every residue field: every minimal prime of the ideal of `2p`-Pfaffians of an alternating `n x n` matrix has height at most `mu(p, n)`, and the depth is at most `mu(p, n)`.
  If the matrix is `9 x 9` (the count 126 equals the number of principal `4 x 4` submatrices of a `9 x 9` matrix, a count the paper does not assert), `mu(2, 9) = 6 * 7 / 2 = 21`. The statement is an upper bound and gives no value for a specialization; equality is the generic case (Corollary 2.5).
- [I] Lemma 1.2 reduces an alternating matrix whose entry `x_12` is invertible to an alternating matrix two sizes smaller with `Pf_(2p)(X) = Pf_(2(p-1))(X')`, by an invertible congruence `C^t X C`; Corollary 1.3 iterates it over a local ring with `Pf_(n-2)(X) = R` to a block normal form.
  Lemma 1.2 is the algebraic form of eliminating a unit entry from a Pfaffian ideal, and it is valid over any commutative ring with identity in which that entry is invertible, so over `Q(i)` and over `F_p`.
  The paper states no transformation rule of a single Pfaffian under congruence; the program's transverse-slice invariance of the Pfaffian ideal (ledger row A5-423) is its own statement.
- [I] What the paper does not give. (a) It does not treat Rees algebras, fiber cones, symbolic powers or integral closure; those statements for the generic ideal are in [Baetica 1998](baetica-1998-rees-algebra-pfaffians.md), which builds on this paper (its Proposition 1.5 uses Lemma 1.2 of this paper). (b) The resolution of Theorem 3.2 is for the ideal of `(n-2)`-Pfaffians with
  2 invertible and depth 6, that is for the ideals of Pfaffians of order `n - 2`; the 4-Pfaffians of a `9 x 9` matrix have order `n - 5`, so Theorem 3.2 does not apply to them, but for `n = 6` it describes `Pf_4(T)`, the Grassmannian `G(2, 6)`. (c) The paper's equality `depth = mu(p, n)` (Theorem 2.3, Corollary 2.5) needs algebraically independent entries over a subring and a flatness hypothesis, so it gives no lower bound on the
  height of a specialization.
